U.K. Charges Two Men Under National Security Act Following Incident at RAF Fairford Airbase

28 Oct 2026, 08:28 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.cbc.ca

British authorities have charged two men with national security offences following a suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford, a military airbase in western England operated by the United States. Police and prosecutors confirmed the charges on Tuesday.

The Crown Prosecution Service stated that Mohmed Abdulkarim, a 24-year-old British-Iranian dual national, and Nouman Essghir, a 24-year-old British citizen, both from London, were charged under the National Security Act. Abdulkarim faces a charge of assisting Iran's intelligence service, while Essghir is accused of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the United Kingdom. Both defendants were scheduled to appear in court on Tuesday.

Investigation and Arrests

The charges stem from an incident on Sept. 27, when armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts deployed to the rural area surrounding RAF Fairford. During the operation, scores of residents were evacuated from their homes while emergency personnel searched for explosives. Authorities later reported recovering a quantity of gasoline and an accelerant from vans at the scene, though no explosives were found.

Essghir was initially arrested outside the base on Sept. 27, released on bail, and subsequently re-arrested. Abdulkarim was taken into custody within the past week. Police noted that six other men have been arrested and released on bail as the ongoing investigation continues.

Official Reactions and Broader Context

British authorities have publicly linked Tehran to the incident at RAF Fairford, a facility that has been utilized by American bombers during recent military engagements. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that the apparent plot was "almost certainly" directed by Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

Conversely, Iran has denied involvement in the incident, maintaining its official stance that any military base utilized to launch attacks against its territory constitutes a legitimate target.

Domestic security officials in the U.K. highlighted a broader pattern of state-backed activity. Ken McCallum, head of the domestic security service, stated that Tehran has sought to intensify attacks in Britain beyond traditional targets involving Iranian dissidents. Officials reported that more than 50 people have been arrested over Iran-linked plots in the U.K. over the past year. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of National Counter Terrorism Policing, affirmed that law enforcement agencies are actively intervening and responding to threats directed by the Iranian state.

In the United States, President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed suspicions regarding Iranian involvement. Following the incident, the U.S. military removed several B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers seeking to verify official statements, legal updates, or announcements regarding this case should consult primary law enforcement and government portals, including the U.K. Crown Prosecution Service and Metropolitan Police.

What is Confirmed Versus Unknown

Confirmed:

  • Two men, Mohmed Abdulkarim and Nouman Essghir, have been charged under the National Security Act.
  • Essghir was arrested outside RAF Fairford on Sept. 27, where police found gasoline and accelerants in vans.
  • U.K. officials have accused Iran's Revolutionary Guard of directing the plot, and the U.S. subsequently relocated bombers from the base.

Unknown:

  • The specific operational details of the alleged plot beyond the initial findings at the scene remain part of an ongoing police investigation.
  • The final legal outcomes of the court proceedings for the two charged individuals and the status of the six other men on bail are yet to be determined.
